james: Hi team — trying to install the private agent in our GKE cluster behind a NAT. Installer fails while fetching wheels and model manifests. Getting SSL cert errors and 403s from our internal artifactory. Can you share a minimal egress allowlist and any OCSP/SNI caveats?

sarah: Sorry about that — can you paste the installer output or a curl from inside the failing pod? Helps us tell TLS vs auth vs IP allowlist.

james: Installer log snippets: 
```
Downloading manifest https://registry.redwood-inference.com/models/rt-2.1/manifest
curl: (35) SSL: certificate verify failed
# pip against our artifactory
pip install --index-url https://acme-artifactory.corp.example/simple/ package-name
403 Client Error: Forbidden for url: https://acme-artifactory.corp.example/simple/package-name/
```
We run split-horizon DNS and company proxy/NAT.

jia: Two quick checks: 1) run curl -v from the exact pod/namespace to both registry and your artifactory, 2) confirm whether your proxy is performing TLS MITM or rewriting SNI for internal hosts (common with split-horizon).

mike: Also capture the certificate presented (openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host>) so we can see subject CN. If the proxy swaps certs you'll see the proxy CN instead of registry CN, and OCSP stapling can break.

james: curl -v inside the pod returns: 
```
$ curl -v https://registry.redwood-inference.com/models/rt-2.1/manifest
* Connected to registry.redwood-inference.com (10.2.3.10) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=corp-proxy.local
* curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
```
Looks like proxy is reissuing certs. Artifactory 403 likely an IP allowlist or missing credentials.

sarah: That matches a TLS interception case. Minimal recommendations: avoid MITM for Redwood hostnames so the cert chain and OCSP work, or if interception is required, add your corp CA to the trust store inside the pod and allow OCSP endpoints. Preferred: bypass MITM for these hostnames.

james: What exact hostnames should we bypass / allow? Want to keep firewall rules restrictive.

jia: Hostname-level allowlist (outbound HTTPS/TCP 443) we recommend:
- registry.redwood-inference.com  (model manifests + control plane)
- model-shards.storage-provider.{region}.amazonaws.com or storage.googleapis.com (actual shard URLs vary by model)
- auth.redwood-inference.com (OAuth / token exchange)
- telemetry.ingest.redwood-inference.com (metrics/usage; optional)
- ocsp.globalsign.com and ocsp.digicert.com (OCSP responders for certificate validation)
- acme-artifactory.corp.example (your internal package registry used by pip)
- kms.redwood-inference.com (if using envelope encryption for model keys)

mike: If your network must use IP-based rules, note these hostnames resolve to multiple region IPs and may shift. We can provide an enterprise metadata endpoint with stable CIDR hints on request. For normal installs prefer SNI/pass-through on the proxy/NAT rather than IP whitelisting.

sarah: Also note ports and protocols: TCP 443 outbound. Allow established connections back in. If you have strict egress proxies, add exception list for registry.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.ingest.redwood-inference.com, and OCSP hosts.

james: For our artifactory 403s — anything Redwood does with headers? We host the artifactory ourselves.

sarah: The installer will not inject auth headers for third-party package hosts. Ensure the pod runs with the expected IP/service account that your artifactory allows, or mount pip credentials in the pod (pip.conf or env vars). A 403 from artifactory usually means auth or IP allowlist on your side, not Redwood.

mike: Another gotcha: if your split-horizon DNS returns internal IPs for registry/artifactory that route through a proxy which swaps certs, pip and the installer can fail. Either bypass proxy for those hostnames or ensure the proxy exposes the original SNI and your internal CA is trusted by the runtime.

james: Any quick probes we can run from the pod to validate OCSP and SNI behavior?

jia: Yes — from the pod: 
```
# check OCSP reachability
curl -I https://ocsp.globalsign.com/gsr || echo "OCSP unreachable"

# SNI and cert check
openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername registry.redwood-inference.com | sed -n '/subject=/,/-/p'
# inspect OCSP stapling
openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername registry.redwood-inference.com -status
```
If subject CN != registry.redwood-inference.com then you're seeing proxy certs. If OCSP responses are missing/staple shows error, that will break strict TLS clients.

james: Ran the openssl check. After adding a proxy bypass for ocsp.globalsign.com and registry.redwood-inference.com, the cert subject shows CN=registry.redwood-inference.com and installer proceeds further.

sarah: Great — sounds like bypass was the right move. If you still hit model shard timeouts/403s after this, share the pod-level curl to the shard URL and the installer full log; we can look at auth tokens and shard ACLs.

mike: For our runbook notes: recommend host-based SNI/pass-through for registry/auth/telemetry + allow OCSP responders + storage provider domains. If a customer requests static IPs escalate to accounts to obtain the signed metadata/CIDR list.

james: Thanks all — we'll roll the bypass in staging and confirm. Will open a ticket if we hit shard errors. :thumbsup:
